title: Copilot Studio: Azure SQL tables and views as an agent knowledge source
notes: claim 72: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, consumption billing and actionable controls are supported. The credit-allocation API exists despite the automatic pre-check's warning; minor corrections should complete the data-policy route, move the API body description into its note and reconcile the checklist with the table. The claim that database reads are live needs narrower wording.

claims.quote: "title": "Microsoft Copilot Studio: SQL server Support in Microsoft Copilot Studio"; "The Azure SQL Knowledge Source capability extends the range of enterprise data sources"

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A Copilot Credit rate specific to Azure SQL knowledge is not published in the documentation checked.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge Copilot Credits rate price. Read billing-credit-overview, manage-usage-github-copilot-harness, knowledge-add-azure-sql-tables and requirements-messages-management search excerpts; no Azure SQL-specific knowledge rate found.

claims.claim: The connector-blocking route is Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Next > three dots > Block.
claims.quote: Select Next. The Add an environment page appears. ... select the environment in the Available tab, and then select Add to policy. ... Select Next. The Assign connectors page appears.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].ui.path and its rendered path with 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Available > environment > Add to policy > Next > connector > ⋮ > Block'. These omitted selections choose the policy scope and connector; the cited page supports the route.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy with PolicyName, Connectors and Classification changes connector classification in a DLP policy.
claims.quote: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy [-PolicyName] <String> [-Classification] <String> [-Connectors] <Object[]> ... Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: applicability paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The checked documentation does not identify an exact connector classification specifically governing Azure SQL knowledge in the Microsoft Copilot experience.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge data policy SQL Server Copilot Studio; SQL Server data policy Blocked connector classification. Read Azure SQL setup, admin-data-loss-prevention, wp-data-loss-prevention and connector comparison; no exact source classification stated.

claims.claim: The printed Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits route reaches environment allocation and tenant-capacity draw.
claims.quote: Under Products, select Copilot Studio, and then select Manage Copilot Credits. ... Under Allocate capacity, enter the number ... Under Capacity overages, select or clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant

claims.claim: PUT licensing/allocationsV2 at version 2024-10-01 sets MCSMessages allocation and disables the TenantPool rule through the printed body properties.
claims.quote: Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put ... -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion" ... scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId } ... entitlementId = "MCSMessages" ... @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call and its rendered call to 'PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01'. Add to the note: 'The body sets scope.environmentId and allocatedEntitlements entries with entitlementId MCSMessages, allocation.quantity and enforcementRules containing ruleType TenantPool and enabled false.' The automatic endpoint warning is a false positive: the article constructs the URL from apiBaseUrl and apiVersion.

claims.claim: Managing capacity requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent licensing-and-capacity role.
claims.quote: Sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: A published environment-group rule prevents an individual environment from overriding tenant-capacity draw.
claims.quote: If a published environment group rule governs Draw from the available capacity in my tenant, you can't override the setting for an individual environment.

claims.claim: Admin-center and API updates governed by the published group rule fail with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: Changing and republishing the group rule or removing the environment from the group permits independent management.
claims.quote: Change and republish the rule for the environment group, or remove the environment from the group to manage the setting independently.

claims.claim: Environment credit controls apply across Copilot Studio workloads, not only Azure SQL knowledge.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: An allocation is not a consumption boundary while tenant capacity or pay-as-you-go remains available.
claims.quote: An allocation isn't a boundary if the environment can continue drawing from tenant capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Disabling tenant-capacity draw does not stop a linked pay-as-you-go billing route.
claims.quote: This setting doesn't prevent consumption through a pay-as-you-go billing plan linked to the environment.

claims.claim: The maker creates or selects a Power Platform SQL connection.
claims.quote: Azure SQL knowledge uses the Power Platform SQL connection you create or select during setup.

claims.claim: Publishing the agent makes the source available in the published experience.
claims.quote: Publish the agent so the knowledge source is available in the published experience.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy
claims.claim: The agent answers questions by reading structured database data using its configured connection and permissions.
claims.quote: Your agent can answer questions by reading structured data from your Azure SQL database, using the configured connection and database permissions.

claims.claim: Views appear in the same selection list as tables.
claims.quote: Views appear in the same selection list as tables. You don't need a separate knowledge source type to add a view.

claims.claim: The SQL connection identity must be permitted to access the database and list and read selected objects.
claims.quote: The identity you use to authenticate the SQL connection must have permission to access the database and list and read the selected tables and views.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Answers are bounded by the data accessible through the maker's configured connection, creating exposure if that access is broad.
claims.quote: Users only receive answers based on data the maker can access through the maker's configured connection and database permissions.

claims.claim: At runtime the agent relies on the agent user's Microsoft authentication and access granted through the connection path.
claims.quote: At runtime, the agent relies on the agent user's Microsoft authentication and the access granted through that connection path.

claims.claim: SQL Server authentication is a documented connection option.
claims.quote: For example, use Microsoft Entra ID or SQL Server authentication, depending on your connection configuration.

claims.claim: For SQL Server authentication, permissions apply to the SQL user specified when creating the connection.
claims.quote: For SQL Server authentication, permissions apply to the SQL user you specify when you create the connection.

claims.quote: Missing or insufficient permissions can prevent servers, databases, tables, or views from appearing during setup.

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Azure SQL knowledge source standard harness credit rate; Azure SQL knowledge Copilot Credits rate price. Read knowledge-add-azure-sql-tables, knowledge-graph-vs-power-platform-connectors and billing pages; no explicit cross-harness qualification found.

claims.where: Why it matters: default and switch; front matter: defaultState
claims.claim: No separate admin switch or explicit rollout default specific to Azure SQL knowledge was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge administrator enable disable default Copilot Studio; Knowledge sources for agents Azure SQL. Read Azure SQL setup, knowledge-add-existing-copilot and knowledge-sources-for-agents-rule; the latter configures SharePoint/OneDrive, public websites and documents, not SQL.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters: automatic rollout
claims.claim: The checked sources do not say Azure SQL knowledge automatically changes existing agent behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge administrator enable disable default Copilot Studio. Read roadmap record, Azure SQL setup and knowledge-sources-overview; these describe adding a source, not automatically attaching it or changing existing agents.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness has no separate maker-access setting.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot harness doesn't have its own maker-access setting.

claims.claim: Authoring access follows existing Copilot Studio and environment permissions, not credit allocations.
claims.quote: To control who can create agents, use your existing Copilot Studio and environment permissions. ... Credit allocations and agent limits control consumption. They don't control who is an approved author

claims.claim: Microsoft suggests testing a diagnostic view with a small known dataset before production data.
claims.quote: Create a diagnostic view in Azure SQL that returns a small, known dataset. ... Test questions about that dataset before using production data.

claims.claim: Configuring the documented agent data policies requires a tenant admin or Environment Admin.
claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.claim: This Microsoft Copilot source reads live business rows.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure SQL knowledge live Microsoft Copilot. Read knowledge-add-azure-sql-tables and knowledge-real-time-connectors. The former states reading structured data; explicit real-time/no-data-movement guarantees on the latter are scoped to the standard harness.
claims.fix: Replace 'The agent reads live business rows through a SQL connection a maker sets up' with 'The agent answers questions by reading structured data through a SQL connection a maker sets up'. Do not carry the standard-harness real-time guarantee into this source.

claims.claim: The governance checklist's controls are all represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Identify ... which makers can edit agents ... Check that makers write a specific knowledge name and description ... Watch credit consumption ... Review agents ... tables and views ... The table gives only connector classification and environment credit allocation.
claims.fix: The maker-permission inventory, knowledge-name/description check, credit-consumption monitoring and selected-table/view review have no table rows. Remove those checklist steps if keeping the current two-row table; this correction requests no additional rows.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Power Platform data policies govern connector access for Copilot Studio agents in the policy's environment scope, covering this source's Power Platform SQL connection.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.claim: The Azure SQL Learn page supplies no rollout date or roadmap release status.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Azure SQL knowledge source admin switch default enable disable connector classification SQL Server knowledge standard harness credit rate. Read knowledge-add-azure-sql-tables in full; it documents setup and permissions without a rollout date or release-status statement.
